description: Every rule here answers one question: which released artifact, or which internal surface,
does this dependency belong to? Without an answer the shared preset's per-update-type
defaults emit feat:/fix:/chore: with the EMPTY scope, a real taxonomy entry ('spans more
than one module, or belongs to none'), so a missing rule does not fail; it silently produces
a header that is in-enum and untrue.
The scope templates read packageFileDir, so a new module directory mints its scope with no
edit here; ci/scripts/commit-taxonomy/ notices when that scope is not yet in the commitlint
enum. See .claude/rules/commits.md for which scope belongs to what.
apps-* subsystem directories: each one is a released module, so its scope is a version claim.
The template takes path segment 2 (apps/subsystems/<name>/...), which is the same key
release-please-config.json maps to the component name -- keep those two in step.
infra-* subsystem directories: as above (infrastructure/subsystems/<name>/...). A bump here
reaches every cluster that pins this module, which is why the scope must name it.
bootstrap CRD copies. LITERAL scope, not a template: path segment 2 here is 'crds', not a
module name, so the apps/infra template above would render 'infra-crds' -- an off-enum scope
that reached production three times (PRs #2327, #2785, #3232) before this rule existed.
shared kustomize components. One collapsed scope rather than component-<name>, because no
component has a version of its own to claim: components ship by proxy, riding each consuming
module's next release. A module scope here would name a release that is not routed, and
the empty scope would hide a real, nameable surface. Per .claude/rules/commits.md scope
rule 5.
this repo's Renovate configuration. The renovate-config manager treats pinned
`github>owner/repo#tag` entries in extends as dependencies, so the bot bumps its preset
pins. Without this rule they fall to the defaults: feat:/fix: with the empty scope, a
shipped claim for a file reaching no cluster.
.github/renovate/** is defensive: unclaimed by the manager today, but must never fall to
the empty scope.
package.json and bun.lock exist only to pin the commitlint the commit gates run; they
reach no cluster, so bumps are chore(internal-dependencies) (.claude/rules/commits.md rule
7). Both managers: bun claims package.json when its lockfile is present. The shared preset
sets the same scope and type for dev depTypes; this rule covers a future 'dependencies'
entry and holds against an in-enum preset rename.
